faq.a: Sunlight has all the colours of the rainbow in it. When it bumps into the air, the blue light bounces around the most, so the whole sky looks blue!
Leaves and grass have a special green helper inside them that catches sunlight to make food for the plant. That helper is green!
The sun warms up water, and it floats up into the sky as tiny drops. They join together to make clouds. When the clouds get too heavy, the water falls down as rain!

q: why do i have to sleep
faq.a: When we sleep, our body and brain rest and grow. Sleep gives us energy to play and learn tomorrow!

q: where does the sun go at night
faq.a: The sun does not go anywhere! Our Earth slowly spins around. When our side turns away from the sun, it becomes night for us.

q: why is the moon changing shape
faq.a: The moon does not really change. We see different parts of it lit by the sun, so sometimes it looks round and sometimes like a banana!
Birds have light bones and strong wings with feathers. They flap their wings to push the air, and up they go!

q: why do we brush our teeth
why should i brush my teeth
faq.a: Brushing cleans away tiny germs and bits of food, so our teeth stay strong and shiny!
Vegetables have vitamins that help us grow tall and strong, and help us fight off coughs and colds!
A rainbow happens when sunlight shines through raindrops. The drops split the light into red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet!
Cats purr when they feel happy and cozy. It is like a cat's way of smiling!
Fish eat tiny plants, little bugs, and special fish food. Some big fish eat smaller fish.

q: why do we have to wash our hands
faq.a: Our hands pick up tiny germs we cannot see. Washing with soap and water sends the germs away, so we stay healthy!
The sun is very, very big! More than a million Earths could fit inside it. It looks small because it is so far away.
The blue whale is the biggest animal ever. It is longer than two buses!
The cheetah is the fastest animal on land. It can run as fast as a car on the highway!
Stars are giant suns, very, very far away. They seem to twinkle because their light wiggles as it travels through our air.
That is a lovely question! Babies grow in a special place inside their mummy's tummy. Your family can tell you more about it.
Bones are like a strong frame inside our body. They help us stand, walk, and keep our heart and brain safe.
Rivers carry tiny bits of salt from rocks into the sea. The salt stays there, so the sea is salty!
